name: Searing Collar
summary: At Skull Rock in Durotar, Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars in their rites. The heated torcs burn their flesh as the cultists attune themselves to demonic power.

sections.title: Instruments of Corruption
sections.body: The Burning Blade gathers for dark rites in Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks, enduring heat that brands and sears their skin. Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects the burning and the enchantments bound to the metal attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do these collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

faq.answer: Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks in rituals. The heated metal burns their flesh and helps attune them to demonic power.
Members of the Burning Blade hiding inside Skull Rock wear the collars, including cultists, fanatics, thugs, apprentices, and neophytes.

faq.q: Why do the cultists burn their own flesh?
faq.answer: The Burning Blade uses the searing metal in its rituals. By enduring the burns and demonic enchantment, cultists attune their bodies and spirits to demonic power.

faq.q: Who wants to inspect the Searing Collars?
faq.answer: Margoz, an investigator camping in Durotar, collects Searing Collars to study their enchantments and uncover the Burning Blade’s influence.

angles.text: As a warlock, you may recognize Searing Collars as crude conduits that channel fel corruption into mortal flesh.
As an orc, finding cultists using these collars on Durotar’s doorstep is a grim reminder that the shadow of demonic servitude still lingers.
